I have Beaten the campaign on Veteran, and played about 1-3 hours of PvP and PvE seperately. Everything stated here was from pre-release, it is still true now.

I think that the campaign for Space Marine 2 is one of my favorites of any game that's come out recently. It really scratches the itch of that classic Gears Trilogy feeling. The way that the characters are written, the interactions between them, the set pieces, the story reveals; everything is just super good. The campaign also does a good job of continuing the story of the first game, while also allowing for new players who never played the first game, to understand this one. The combat-loop can feel a bit repetitive, but it's broken up with boss fights, different factions, and other mechanics that make it feel fresh as the campaign continues.

The post-campaign PvE, and PvP, are both a blast, and I think there is a ton of potential for them as the game continues to get content updates. The progression is really good, and the customization makes it feel like I can bring all the customizing of an actual painted miniature, into the game, with all the available options. The leveling being separate between the modes kind of blows, but I think this is due to a technical limitation because of how the separate modes are loaded. Customization carries over, so i'm not too upset about it.

Some of my main complaints with the game, are more technical than mechanics. Not only my CPU, but my friends' CPUs, have all been running really hot while playing this game, even when in the menus. It sits at around 75-80 degrees C, even if I'm just in the menu. All of the CPUs are different, and their workloads are never super high. That is a major concern for me. Aside from that main issue, I think we need a shoulder POV swap option, and an FOV slider, for different accessibility reasons.

TLDR; If you have an interest in this game, and liked playing the original Gears of War games, I totally recommend giving this game a go. I had a blast, and I'm sure you will too.

reviews.review: I love this game, it is intense to its core, campaign could have been longer. I would like to note, that as a PC player, joining sessions, connecting to the server, is a constant issue when completing missions or continuing after completing missions, players from console get disconnected easy or the parties end up solo.

Space Marine 2 is absolutely fantastic.  If you are a fan of third person action games along the lines of Gears of War, Remnant, etc or enjoy games set in the Warhammer 40K setting like Darktide - you won't be disappointed here.  Production value is top notch, the epic scale is there, there's a core campaign with a co-op option, there's a set of repeatable co-op missions using your own custom space marine that logically fits with the campaign, and there's a PVP mode if that's of interest to you.  Highly recommended, and I hope we see DLC with more missions (core campaign and/or co-op).

This is a game for which the yes/no review scale really doesn't work well.

I played through the campaign in around 8.5 hours. It's not all that long, but I don't mind that. What I do mind is that I was quite bored by the end of it. The combat system feels good at first, but never develops or progresses, so it ends up quite shallow. Enemy variety is pitiful, making combat even more repetitive. Guns feel weedy. This may be to push players into more melee combat, but it still feels out of keeping with the setting.

The story moves along at a decent clip. There are some decent set-pieces and the character beats, while somewhat repeated from the first game, basically work. It's not the most sophisticated take on the WH40K universe. It's basically "OOH RAH SPACE MARINES", which would be disappointing at the best of times, but feels a bit sinister with a Russian developer. Your regularly scheduled reminder - the Imperium are not the good guys.

Visually, it does the minimum necessary. There visual design has a few good moments, but it's weird for a major 2024 release to have no ray tracing and be 100% rasterisation. The lighting looks flat and artificial throughout.

I didn't dislike the game, but it's nothing special. It's a short, shallow corridor shooter with some decent WH40K trappings. I've given it the thumbs up because it is very slightly more good than bad, but overall... wait for a sale.

Up front: this game has some technical issues I should warn about, I know some people have had a much harder time making it run than me, so know that going in. I have faith this team can fix a lot of that, though. This is the WWZ team and it's built on a lot of the same tech (I think), and that game had great long-term support, both with content and performance/QOL patches. I'd also say play the campaign co-op if you can: it makes things go a lot smoother. Your companion AI isn't great and you don't have any way of directing them. The action is fun and the missions are well paced, especially once you get into the new rhythm of mixing melee with ranged combat (which is more necessary this time around). About combat: once you get the opportunity to switch to Operations Mode, do so and play the Trials for every class. Not only does it reward you with currency for it, it teaches some important tips better than the actual campaign does (like reminding you how to fight some enemies or how to be a good Brother). There's a whole year of free stuff coming, including a horde mode (love me a good horde mode), so it's a great deal at $60 for a beefy, fun campaign and good co-op action. The multiplayer classes rule. The season pass is exclusively more cosmetics, so if you wanna be a specific chapter you might have to pay, but you can skip it if making a cool looking guy is less important to you.

This is a conflicted review tbh, On one hand I love the game, and on the other I really hate some of the systems, so I'm gonna try and attempt to break those things down here.

Story,
The story is relatively short, but as far as I'm concerned it does exactly what It needed, and is a blast visually and audibly, even when there were things happening that I didn't understand from lack of context it was still fun and interesting enough to keep my attention and push forward, 8/10

Combat,
This is both awful and amazing, on the good side it feels, sounds, and looks great, but the actual motion of going through combat isn't good at all, the main problem is that there is no reliable way to heal, so lets break it down, the only ways to heal are. Stims, Retaliation, and being revived. So what's wrong with this? Well there aren't enough stims to keep you alive and going, nor does the Bloodborne inspired mechanic of retaliation work when there are multiple mobs all hitting you thus stopping any gain back you might get, Well what about just resetting with a revive? That doesn't work either because after getting knocked twice you will permanently die in the campaign, or you re-spawn after 1 minute in COOP.

Now all that doesn't seem so bad, but it leads to frustration all around, you will die, a lot, all the time, and it will feel cheap, because as you move through the maps you will get damaged, and eventually (especially on harder difficulties) you'll die, and you'll keep dying because there is no way to fully heal after or during encounters, so no matter what you will get chipped down and die, now I know people would say well that's what the armor mechanic is for, but that at best let's you brush off 3 hits, while this helps, and lets you maintain yourself in combat it's just not enough to keep you up and going.

I would like to mention this is primarily a campaign problem, then it lessens in COOP due to perks you can get with certain classes and is probably non existent in PVP.

In total 5/10, and if we get some kind of alternative way to heal later on as they patch and maintain the game I'd give it a 9/10.

I'm gonna end it there, in total I'd say this is a easy recommend if you like this kind of game, overall I'd say it's worth it just for the story and a fun campaign at lower difficulties.

I love this game so far, but I have a few thoughts that I think really need to be addressed (and not many people are talking about it). First, I know people complain about difficulty, but after only a few hours, I started learning the nuances of melee and the attack patterns of a lot of the warrior and up enemies. Since then, the ebb and flow and attack strategy of my own character became way more comfortable (and cool as hell). Of course there needs to be some balance changes, like a perk on the assault class that heals your main health slightly as well when completing a finisher. 

BUT, FOR THE LOVE OF THE EMPEROR, the control scheme for mouse and keyboard is horrible and there is no setup that I've found that isn't uncomfortable or isn't actively fighting my muscle memory for every other game I've ever played. People say use controller, and yes, that is my currently preferred option, but I would love to use mouse and keyboard if the way they implemented controls didn't want me to rip my hair out.

The main issue - there is no good mix of melee, aim, and shooting buttons that doesn't explode my brain trying to get use to. What should happen - and there should be an option to allow this - default left click is melee, and use right click to aim your weapon, BUT when aiming, left click changes to "shoot". Yes you'd lose the ability to "hipfire" but it's extremely rare you'll be doing that, that often anyways. This change alone would improve the ebb and flow between melee and shooting. All other keybinds aren't an issue because there are plenty of options for that, but by the emperor am I losing my mind whenever I even attempt to use mouse and keyboard.

Last thing, allow the "press" of a button vs. the "hold" of a button be mapped to different things.

Other than that, the depth of this game is amazing and there is definitely a skill issue for most, including myself. Here are some things i've learned so far - If you're on sniper, stop shooting small mobs and try to make every shot a headshot, otherwise it's a waste of ammo. Most classes, ff you are surrounded and are using a weapon that can, for emperors sake use your heavy stomp. Tactical, heavy, or basically anyone, shoot enemies using ranged weapons first or chase them down. Controlling melee fights is doable but ranged damage can easily get out of control. It is paramount they die asap and should always be a priority before charging in against a melee horde. In short, I think everyone also needs to remember that we're playing space marines. Yeah they're large and covered in heavy metal, but space marines are smart, strong, and fast as hell. Lore wise, what we're doing as a squad of three shouldn't really be feasible lol, but it is possible once you realize that this game expects you to play as though you could. Become the emperors finest I know you can be.

TLDR - Control schemes need an overhaul, expect to suck early (don't force higher difficulties), especially when first leveling a class and weapon, and know that you're expected to become the most efficient killing machine the Imperium of man has to offer. You're a space marine, act like it.
